description: Team Anno Domini is building Anno Ignis---a harmonized 26-year chronicle of Earth's active fires (2000-2026).By fusing NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite datasets through spatiotemporal clustering , we eliminate sensor resolution bias to reveal true multi-decade fire trends and El-Niño climate impacts.
summary:
ANNO IGNIS is a satellite-based fire intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, focusing on harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations. The project aims to address differences between these satellite sensors by improving the consistency and comparability of their fire detection data through data preprocessing, quality screening, spatial and temporal analysis, and statistical harmonization.

The platform brings satellite observations together to support comparative analysis, interactive fire mapping, historical trend exploration, and regional fire monitoring. By making observations from different sensors more comparable, ANNO IGNIS aims to provide a clearer and more consistent understanding of global fire activity.

This project is important because reliable satellite fire information supports environmental monitoring, wildfire research, and informed decision-making. ANNO IGNIS demonstrates how harmonized Earth observation data can help transform multiple satellite datasets into more meaningful and accessible insights.
details:
Project Details

ANNO IGNIS is a satellite-based fire intelligence platform focused on harmonizing NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations. It aims to address differences between satellite sensors and make their fire detection data more consistent, comparable, and useful for environmental monitoring.

How It Works

The project uses satellite observations from MODIS (Terra and Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21). Its workflow involves satellite data ingestion, preprocessing, data quality screening, spatial and temporal analysis, and statistical harmonization. The resulting data can support sensor comparisons, fire activity visualization, regional analysis, and historical trend exploration.

Benefits and Intended Impact

By improving the comparability of observations from different satellite sensors, ANNO IGNIS aims to provide more reliable insights into fire activity. It can support wildfire research, environmental monitoring, and better interpretation of satellite-derived fire information. Its intended impact is to make multi-sensor fire observations easier to analyze and more useful for understanding global fire patterns.

Tools and Technologies

The project uses:

  • Programming Language: Python
  • Data Processing: Pandas, NumPy, SciPy
  • Visualization: Plotly, Folium
  • Application Framework: Streamlit
  • Data Source: NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS observations)

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of ANNO IGNIS lies in bringing observations from different satellite sensors into a common analytical framework. Instead of treating MODIS and VIIRS as separate data sources, the project focuses on harmonization to improve their comparability and enable more meaningful combined analysis.

Factors Considered

During development, the team considered differences in sensor characteristics, spatial resolution, observation timing, data quality, missing values, and the challenges of comparing satellite observations. Data accessibility, processing efficiency, and clear visualization were also important considerations.

ANNO IGNIS aims to demonstrate how harmonized satellite observations can contribute to more consistent fire intelligence and improved understanding of Earth's changing environment.
